versionNote: catalogueVersion is the CONTENT revision - BUMP IT whenever the shipped lineup changes, or the update cannot reach an install that already seeded %APPDATA%/Dwight/models.json (the user copy wins). On a bump, the existing user copy is preserved aside as models.v<old>.bak and the new catalogue is written; edit the refreshed file and it wins again. schemaVersion is the FORMAT and moves only on a breaking shape change.
note: Dwight model catalogue (October 2026 refresh, #910-#912; every fact sourced to a vendor page in the PR 'Model catalogue - October 2026'). Single source of truth for ids, prices, tiers and capabilities (ADR-081). User-editable copy at %APPDATA%/Dwight/models.json - add a model the day it ships, drop one your key cannot call, or correct a price; no recompile. Prices USD per 1M tokens (in/out), the vendor's standard tier for prompts under its long-context threshold; a time-limited price is recorded as the price in force today with its end date in speedNote. The Advanced 'Check models' reconciler marks each green/amber/red against YOUR key - the reconciler, not this file, is the authority on what you can actually call. Tiers Fast/Mid/Strong/Top are capability bands the resolver maps tasks to (ADR-082); the profile only slides within a task's band. The bands are the catalogue's own judgement, not a vendor fact. Context windows: the vendor's stated figure; Ollama's 'nK' is n*1024 and its '1M' is recorded as 1000000.
statusNote: status: stable = the vendor lists it active; preview = the vendor labels it preview (reconciles amber, not red, when a key cannot list it); confirm = the id is unverified against a live list; retired = the vendor has retired the id. A retired model is KEPT, never deleted - a user's Settings may still name it, and the reconciler is what tells them (it reconciles red). Retired entries carry preference 90 so they can never win a band tie before the reconciler has run.
cachePriceNote: priceCachedIn and priceCacheWrite are USD per 1M tokens from the vendor's own page, named with its date in cachePriceSource, and the cost reads them. A row with neither uses Anthropic's ratio (x0.10 read, x1.25 write) as an estimate. A time-limited price is the one in force today, with its end date in cachePriceSource. Past ledger lines keep the cost they were written with.
capabilityNote: structuredOutput=reliable schema-constrained output (the structured gate). vision (Brief DX)=the vendor's page says this model takes image input; the Build chat's attach refuses by name on a row without it, and absent reads as false, so a row added by hand refuses until it says so. imagePatchTokens=this row counts an image as ceil(width / 28) x ceil(height / 28) + 3: Anthropic's page says it of Claude 4.7 and later, and it was measured on Sonnet 5.5. Only such a row shows a number on the image's chip; every other says the provider counts it, because Gemini 3.8 Flash and qwen3.5:9b measured 1,064 and 1,820 where this rule says 2,355, and Anthropic's older rows are capped. reasoning=has a thinking mode; reasoningKnob=its depth is adjustable. thinkingDefault (#192)=what OMITTING the thinking field does: 'adaptive-on' means thinking RUNS unless explicitly disabled (the Claude 5 family), 'adaptive-off' means omitting is off, 'none' means Dwight never sends a thinking field. A model whose only thinking mode is the retired fixed budget_tokens budget is 'none' - Dwight does not carry two thinking dialects, and such models sit in Fast bands that no thinking-on task reaches. Non-Anthropic providers are 'none' because the field this fact describes is Anthropic's thinking block: OpenAI's Responses wire carries a reasoning effort (reasoningKnob), never a thinking field, and Google and Ollama get no reasoning field at all. agentic (#189, ENFORCED by #884)=may be handed the agent loop; true ONLY where the model is documented to call tools AND Dwight's connection to its provider carries them (a test holds every true row to the provider's PassesTools). The Fast band and models of 8B or fewer stay false (#189), so a small model is never silently handed Scaffold. Today that is Anthropic (Sonnet and Opus class), OpenAI (Mid and above), Ollama Cloud (the Mid and above models whose library page lists tools) and Ollama local (the 9B-and-larger models whose library page lists tools) and Google (Strong and above).
excludedNote: #910, paid by Brief BZ on 2026-10-31: Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1 are now listed, with per-model facts instead of an exclusion: thinking off as omit plus low effort (Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1) or between_tools (Sonnet 5.5), and a verb's shape through output_config.format. pinOnly keeps every resolver away from a row, whatever its band or price: Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 until a gate measures them, and Fable 5.1 for good. agentic stays by measurement.
preferenceNote: preference (#199) breaks a tie when two models match on BAND and on PRICE - lower wins, absent reads as 100 (neutral). It exists because Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 4.6 were both Strong at $3/$15: without it the winner fell out of the order these lines happen to sit in, so reordering two lines would silently move every Strong task to a different model. Resolution order is band distance, then price, then this, then the id - never file position. Convention: 10 = the current generation in its band, 50 = the retained previous generation, 90 = retired.
